description: Account-scoped cPanel integration links and groups, and server-wide script/Perl hook inventory and management. Configuration, tokens, URLs and hook command payloads may be private. The client does not activate links, fetch returned URLs or invoke hooks; changes are single requests without retry or rollback.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 54 and later.

The group belongs to the explicitly supplied cPanel account. Supplying an existing group_id replaces the existing group. The source warns about replacement using create-link wording; no merge behavior is promised.
order is a required integer with documented minimum 1. The source notes that an item is automatically created under the username menu in the interface header. No data payload is documented.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 54 and later.

The link belongs to the explicitly supplied cPanel account. An existing app value replaces that link. The server creates APP.adminconfig and APP.userconfig under /var/cpanel/integration/links/USERNAME; no client-side file access occurs.

implements is the caller-supplied service string from get_users_links. The listed billing, customer_service, support and upgrade services are typical examples, not a closed enum. group_id keeps the documented built-in group choices. order is a string; it is not converted to an integer.

Supply autologin_token_url, url, or both. If the autologin endpoint is absent or unavailable, the server redirects the user to url. The server may POST app, token, user and subscriber_unique_id to the autologin endpoint and process redirect_url or retry/attempt responses; this client only configures the link and never fetches either URL.

Omitted hide defaults to 0 (display the link); true sends 1 (hide). Omitted group_id places the item under the username menu. Omitted base64_png_image uses a puzzle-piece icon; supplied image data stays an unchanged string and is not decoded or rendered.

Token and URL arguments may contain credentials and are sensitive. No data payload is documented. Replacement and later link use can affect authentication behavior; the client does not retry or roll back the request.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11.32 and later.

This edits a server-wide hook identified by listHooks(). exectype selects script or module; hook is the absolute script path or module::subroutine invocation. Module hooks call a Perl module and cannot escalate privileges.

enabled controls whether the hook is enabled. Omitted escalateprivs defaults to 0 and applies only to script hooks; true runs the script as root. stage pre runs before the triggering function and post runs after it. Lower weight runs earlier within the stage; the documented minimum is 1.

check runs after the hook to check its results; rollback identifies the rollback script. The hook, check and rollback strings may contain private command information and remain sensitive. Editing may cause commands to run when later events trigger the hook; this client does not invoke them automatically.

Omitted options retain server behavior. The rollback parameter names an upstream hook script, not a client transaction guarantee. No data payload is documented; the client performs one request with no retry or automatic rollback.

The specified app and explicit cPanel account select the user configuration. The pinned source marks this retrieval x-readonly=false, so it uses form POST.

Returned userconfig URL, image, subscriber and account values are payload data and may be private. URLs are returned without fetching them, and image strings are not decoded or rendered. Optional fields remain omitted; null is not inferred for documented strings.

The app parameter repeats a create-link replacement warning in the pinned text. This retrieval does not create a link; the source inconsistency is retained here without inferring a write or an extra request.

This lists server-wide hook categories, events, stage order, stages, attributes and actions. Action check, description and rollback fields explicitly allow null; other omitted fields remain omitted. Flags retain native integer 0/1 values and weights retain integers.
Hook paths, command/module text and descriptions are private payload data. No hook script, check script, rollback script or returned URL is executed or fetched by the client.

The thirteen action leaf types are restored from the original pinned schema because the effective schema expansion depth limit otherwise yields mixed at that depth. Only the explicitly nullable check, description and rollback fields permit null; this is source coverage, not live normalization.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11.32 and later.

ids is caller-serialized comma-separated hook IDs in priority order, obtained from listHooks(). It remains an unchanged string encoded once as a form field; the client does not invent repeated keys, array encoding or JSON serialization.

The pinned hook_order node omits type but documents a list, declares object items and shows an array example. The reviewed correction makes it a list with optional string id and integer weight fields. Lower weight has greater priority; no numeric-string normalization is inferred.
This changes the server-wide hook order and does not invoke hooks. The client does not retry or automatically restore the previous order.
